Only ecosystems whose registry version is the commit that changed a recipe file are matched by the recipe's bytes; every other recipe-in-git registry (opam-repository, the Bazel Central Registry, CocoaPods Specs, Julia's General) gives each release a version of its own, so a verdict on one is matched by name and version like any package.

Only Packagist and RubyGems mark a withdrawn release by dropping it from their public version list; every other registry marks a withdrawal explicitly (yanked, unlisted, deprecated), which is read where it is published.

The registries a cross-registry confusion probe borrows names from are the bare-word ones whose names are published unscoped and unqualified (npm and crates.io by default, PyPI and RubyGems from npm); this is each adapter's declaration of which of those its own names can collide with, and a name established in the ecosystem itself is never compared.
npm's own declaration of the bare-word registries whose established names an empty npm package borrows in a confusion probe (PyPI, RubyGems, crates.io), as nokogiri, wasm-bindgen and pyrefly were.

The formats whose installer itself can run make on any package (R's src/Makefile, elixir_make, a gem's extconf.rb, cabal's build-type: Make); in every other ecosystem a Makefile is install-time code exactly when the package's own install hook, setup.py, build.rs or binding.gyp starts make, which InstallRunsMake reads per package.
Workflows and container builds run only in a repository's own automation, never for a package's installer, so their dependencies are scoped to the repository alone.
Cargo and Julia's [compat] read a bare version as a caret range; every other ecosystem reads a bare version as exact.
